text:
anna: Hey all — running into a weird SSE streaming failure in production. App sees malformed JSON sometimes after an abrupt connection close (TCP FIN from upstream). Python client recovers; Node client returns a partial message. Anyone seen this? :eyes:

miguel: Yup, sounds like a chunk boundary + resume race. Do you have raw fragments/logs?

anna: Pasting a sanitized raw capture from the client (we log raw SSE frames):
```
data: {"seq":1,"delta":"Hello "}\n
data: {"seq":2,"delta":"wor"
```
Server FINs here, client reconnects and new connection yields:
```
data: {"seq":3,"delta":"ld"}\n
```
Combined result becomes invalid JSON when reassembled by Node parser.

tom: That first fragment cuts in the middle of a token ("world"). Node SDK's streaming parser currently treats a final stream end as "flush and emit what we have". If a fragment ends mid-json it tries to parse and fails, whereas Python buffers until a complete event (final newline) before emitting.

jen: Two related vectors we've seen: (1) auth refresh triggers client abort+reconnect which can cut frames mid-event, (2) proxy/idle timeouts (nginx, envoy) that send RST/FIN on long idle connections. Both lead to partial last-event.

miguel: Workarounds: ensure server always emits a final newline after an event and include an explicit per-event seq or resume token in a header or data field. Client-side, make parsers tolerant: buffer partial data across reconnects keyed by resume-token/last-event-id.

anna: I built a tiny repro server (node) that randomizes FIN mid-event — gist: https://gist.github.com/example/repro-sse (sanitized). Test run shows node-sdk fails ~7% when forced FIN at 30-70% through message.

tom: For parity: we should add a unit/integration test in sdk-tests that runs the repro server and asserts both SDKs reassemble correctly. Node SDK change suggestion: don't emit on end-of-stream if the last event doesn't end with a newline; instead mark as "incomplete" and attempt resume if possible.

jen: Also check auth token refresh flow: when refresh happens mid-stream the client currently cancels request then opens a new one without attempting to stitch partials. We should either pause refresh until a safe boundary or make stitch logic resilient.

anna: Proposal:
- Add flaky CI test that exercises abrupt FINs + auth refresh combos (node + python).
- Spec: streaming semantics doc update: servers must flush newline for complete events; clients must buffer partial events and use resume token/last-event-id semantics to reconcile duplicates/gaps.
- Short-term workaround: enable regular heartbeat (15s) to prevent idle proxies closing, and turn on reconnect backoff jitter in prod clients.

miguel: I'll add the CI job and a test harness. @tom can you own the Node SDK test + parser tweak? @jen can you file a short RFC and open an issue for auth-refresh behavior?

tom: On it — will open PR with parser change and tests. Quick patch: treat trailing buffer without newline as unparseable, stash by resume-token, and attempt merge on reconnect.

deploy-bot: CI job created: nightly/sse-abrupt-close-resume-race (flaky).

jen: Filed issue #5123 in repo: "SDK: streaming reassembly on abrupt close and auth refresh" with links to logs and repro. :white_check_mark:

anna: Thanks everyone. Will monitor customer and add an entry to devex troubleshooting guide about this kind of failure. For the short term, recommending apps set heartbeat + idempotent partial handling. :thumbsup:
